## A. Transient and time-varying shunt stress over the full model class

Let K_0 be a symmetric positive definite irreducible M-matrix, C a fixed known
positive diagonal matrix, b=e_0 and K_1=K_0+delta e_v e_v^T, delta>0. Initially
x_h(0)=0. For a common input u(t) and a nonnegative diagonal shunt schedule
D(t), consider

    C xdot_h = -(K_h+D(t))x_h + b u(t),   y_h=b^T x_h.

Assume D is piecewise continuous, or locally integrable where the fundamental
solutions exist. The schedule may be arbitrarily fast and arbitrarily large;
giving it for free only strengthens the attempted alternative. C is fixed,
and changing C without the corresponding physical balance terms is not in
this model. The input may have either sign and belongs to L2.

Write A_h(t)=-C^{-1}(K_h+D(t)), P=delta C^{-1}e_v e_v^T>=0, and let
U_h,D(t,s) be its state transition. These transitions are entrywise nonnegative
because the generators are Metzler. Variation of constants gives

    U_0,D(t,s)-U_1,D(t,s)
      = integral_s^t U_0,D(t,r) P U_1,D(r,s) dr >= 0.          (A1)

Adding a nonnegative diagonal loss also gives

    0 <= U_h,D(t,s) <= exp[-C^{-1}K_h(t-s)]                   (A2)

entrywise, by the same variation-of-constants comparison with D=0. Substituting
both bounds into the positive product in (A1) yields

    0 <= k_D(t,s) <= k_0(t-s),                              (A3)

where k_D=b^T(U_0,D-U_1,D)C^{-1}b is the difference of the two port impulse
kernels and k_0 is the unloaded difference kernel. This is a pointwise kernel
claim, stronger than comparing a few pulses. Both systems are exponentially
stable without D; positive D preserves the comparison and cannot cause growth.

The positive integrable kernel k_0 has total mass

    integral_0^infinity k_0(t)dt
      = b^T(K_0^{-1}-K_1^{-1})b = Delta_DC.                  (A4)

For every signed u, including under a time-varying schedule,

    |y_0(t)-y_1(t)| <= (k_0 * |u|)(t),
    ||y_0-y_1||_2 <= Delta_DC ||u||_2.                       (A5)

The last step is Young's convolution inequality. With D=0 the induced L2 gain
is exactly Delta_DC: the Fourier transform obeys |Delta G(iw)|<=Delta_DC,
with equality at w=0, and arbitrarily long slowly varying inputs approach
that gain. This is the scalar positive-system result in Rantzer's established
Theorem 3. It is not a newly discovered general control principle.

## Q63 — DECISIVE NEGATIVE retained; capacity-anchored reconstruction is valid

The original target remains useful recovery of inaccessible network structure with one boundary sensor. Stage2 strengthens the failure boundary and adds a genuine conditional exact operation. Governing evidence: [PROOF_STAGE2.md](/Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/coordination/work/astra-method-experiment-20261026/review_material/Q63/stage2/PROOF_STAGE2.md), [stress_and_completion.py](/Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/coordination/work/astra-method-experiment-20261026/review_material/Q63/stage2/stress_and_completion.py), [finite_pulse_acquisition.py](/Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/coordination/work/astra-method-experiment-20261026/review_material/Q63/stage2/finite_pulse_acquisition.py), and [RESULT.md](/Users/harjas/Documents/ChatGPT/coordination/work/astra-method-experiment-20261026/review_material/Q63/stage2/RESULT.md).

The positive-cascade comparison is sound. Metzler transition matrices remain nonnegative; inserting nonnegative time-dependent diagonal losses decreases both factors of the fault cascade. Consequently its kernel is bounded by the unloaded positive convolution kernel, whose mass is the unloaded DC fault difference. Young's inequality gives the claimed all-signed-input L2 bound. For finite sampled operators, entrywise order bounds the spectral norm, so unloaded SVD is an equally informed optimum over the same waveform class. The adaptive white-readout KL bound follows along common observation histories under the stated existence/integrability and pathwise input-budget assumptions. Its resource is **integral squared input**, not actual dissipated energy or a full reset/source budget.

The separate quasistatic variance model a+nu F is handled correctly. The admittance argument decreases both absolute and relative fault contrast. This decreases the mean and covariance terms of both Gaussian KL directions. It is a KL result, not an unequal-variance Blackwell theorem. No full colored-noise or general thermodynamic inference follows from the extra frequency grid. [Rantzer, Theorem 3](https://arxiv.org/html/1203.0047v3) was read and already supplies the positive LTI static-gain fact; the time-varying fault specialization is derived locally.
